title: A profile anchor the validator accepts and the renderer cannot resolve crashes lore agent context with an uncaught exit 1
description:
Found by the LCLI-642 adversarial review (2026-09-29, reviewer report F1), in code this session did not write but did make reachable from a required CI context. DEFECT: `validateAgentProfileReferences` accepts an anchored profile reference whose heading the PACK RENDERER cannot resolve, and the renderer then throws a plain `Error` -- not a `LoreError` -- which the CLI reports as `{"error_type":"uncaught"}` with exit 1 and ZERO bytes of stdout. MECHANISM: `src/core/agent-profile.ts`'s `headingSlugs` walks every mdast node (`walkMdast`), while `src/core/agent-context.ts`'s `regionForReference` scans only TOP-LEVEL headings (`tree.children.filter(child => child.type === "heading")`). A heading nested in a blockquote, a list item or a footnote is therefore visible to the validator and invisible to the renderer. A plain typo on a `member::id`-qualified reference triggers it too, because the validator deliberately skips qualified references entirely. REPRODUCED (four shapes, verified through the real CLI on identical fixture bytes): an anchor on a heading inside a blockquote; an anchor whose plain slug a blockquoted duplicate heading shifts (`# Overview` inside a quote steals the slug, moving the real `## Overview` to `overview-1`); an anchor on a heading inside a list item; and `sources = ["other-member::reference/big#no-such-heading"]`. Each makes `bun run lore agent context

--task ...` exit 1 with `validated heading disappeared: ` and an empty stdout, where the contract reserves exit 1 for "the command broke" (cli-contract §5.1) and `lore check --help` advertises only 0, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED IN LCLI-642: LCLI-642's check now DECLINES such a profile (counted `unmeasurable`) instead of letting the throw escape into `lore check`, because `lore check` is a required CI context and exiting 1 with no report is worse than not measuring. That is a guard at the new call site, not a repair: `lore agent context` still exits 1 on the same profiles, and the validator still accepts an anchor the renderer cannot honour. The repair belongs where the two disagree, and it needs a ruling on which side is right -- whether a nested heading SHOULD be a valid anchor target (in which case `regionForReference` is the bug) or the validator should reject what the renderer cannot resolve (in which case `headingSlugs` is) -- because the answer changes the profile contract for every consuming repository.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The disagreement is settled by a recorded decision, not by choosing a side in code: either a nested heading is a valid anchor target for a profile reference (renderer fixed) or it is not (validator fixed), with the reasoning on the record

Both sides of the chosen behaviour are covered: an anchor the renderer can resolve still compiles, and an anchor it cannot is rejected by `lore agent context` as a classifiable `LoreError` with an exit code the contract advertises, rather than an uncaught exit 1 with empty stdout

A regression test reproduces at least the blockquote-nested and the qualified-typo shapes from the LCLI-642 review, and fails against the pre-fix build in the same invocation (the pre-fix run must show the uncaught exit 1 and empty stdout)
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0
